transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-08-25 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Altair VP Platform), Liam O'Connell (Altair SRE Lead), Priya Rao (Altair Procurement), Ethan Brooks (Altair ML)

Summary: quick recap at top, then conversational transcript follows. Some auto-summaries may be wrong.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll jump into the proposed amendment and capacity numbers.
[00:12] Maya: Hey Samir, hey Lena, thanks. We've got about 45 minutes. Liam and I will cover SRE concerns, Priya on procurement.
[00:22] Lena: Great. I'll lead the tech portion — quick reminder, playbook is around committed tokens, dedicated pods for tail-latency, and EU onboarding steps.
[00:35] Liam: Quick thing up front — primary ask is that the EU region provisioning keeps 99th percentile latency under 150ms for our inference path, that's the bar for our customer-facing flows.
[00:50] Samir: Understood. Our standard dedicated plan with the latency SLA plus canary routing to hosted fallback should keep you under that; we'll show historical fixtures in the benchmark.
[01:05] Ethan: When you say fallback, is the KV cache preserved across fallback? We can't have large cold-start regressions.
[01:18] Lena: Good call — K-V cache is per model instance and we have prefix caching for hot keys. On fallback to hosted we'll do a warm-warm handoff where possible but there can be a short spike, that's part of the SLA docs.
[01:37] Maya: Also need to be explicit about data residency — EU region must not leave the EU for inference logs or token storage.
[01:47] Carlos: Yep, we'll include data routing policy in the amendment: logs and unredacted traces stay in the customer VPC in EU, option for a private control plane.
[02:00] Priya: On the procurement side, timeline check — we'll need a signed amendment and PO before Sept 15 to hit our Q4 budget window.
[02:10] Samir: Targeting to send that by Friday (2026-08-27). We'll include a price table for committed tokens and an option for burst capacity.
[02:25] Maya: What does burst cost look like? Our traffic pattern is spiky during EMEA business hours.
[02:33] Lena: Burst is metered at a premium (we price bursts as 1.6x the committed unit rate); however, if you enable autoscaling policies with pre-warmed reserved capacity we can lower that to about 1.2x for planned spikes.
[02:48] Liam: Can you elaborate on pre-warmed reserved capacity? Is that basically dedicated pool that sits idle? Cost tradeoff?
[02:58] Lena: It's a reserved capacity bucket that can be assigned to your region and warmed to maintain KV and warm threads. You pay a lower hourly commitment; it reduces cold-start latency and KV misses. We can model a 10% reserved pool vs just burst and show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:18] Ethan: For our NLU models we use long context windows; does the kernel selection and quantization affect tail latency? We need to avoid quality regressions.
[03:30] Lena: We select kernels by architecture and seq length distribution. Quantization profiles are optional; for your production models we'd recommend 8-bit quant for throughput but we'll run quality evals against your eval set first.
[03:45] Maya: SOC2 and encryption — is KMS integration available with a customer-managed key? We need proof for audits.
[03:54] Carlos: Yes, KMS/HSM support is in Private and Dedicated. We'll share the integration guide and the SOC2 artifacts.
[04:05] Priya: Please include an explicit clause that Redwood will provide audit logs for all admin ops for the contract term.
[04:12] Samir: Noted, we'll add admin audit logs retention and access controls to the amendment.
[04:20] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[04:23] Liam: One more thing — can we run an A/B canary for an hour against 10% of traffic in EU staging to validate latencies?
[04:32] Lena: Absolutely. We'll schedule a 60 to 90 minute run with synthetic and real-ish traffic. We'll capture 50th/95th/99th percentiles and token cost metrics.
[04:44] Maya: What's the expected lead time to stand up EU staging under Dedicated? We need pre-prod mirrors.
[04:52] Samir: Typically 2–3 weeks from signed amendment to EU staging, 4–6 weeks to full production if there are no infra blockers. If you opt for private control plane that adds an extra week for the VPC peering and audit.
[05:07] Ethan: Do you support VPC peering or direct connect equivalents for throughput-sensitive traffic?
[05:15] Lena: Yes VPC peering and we have marketplace connectors. For on-prem you'd use the private connector and optionally HSM.
[05:25] Priya: On pricing appendix — can you give us two scenarios: (A) committed + small reserved pool + bursts; (B) larger commit with lower per-token price, minimal bursts. We want to compare CAPEX vs OPEX style impacts.
[05:39] Samir: We'll produce both. We'll include a simple cost-per-1M-token breakout and a modeled monthly invoice for your current and forecasted traffic.
[05:50] Maya: SLA penalties — what does the SLA credit look like if you miss the 99th percentile SLA?
[05:57] Carlos: Standard credits: pro-rata credit up to one month of service for repeated SLA misses. We'll attach the SLA clause.
[06:08] Liam: Can you provide a runbook for incident escalation and on-call handoff when there's regional degradation?
[06:16] Samir: Yes, Carlos will attach the runbook. Our standard escalation is 15-min initial ack, 60-min remediation plan, and RTO/RCA windows documented.
[06:29] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:33] Lena: For model rollouts — if you pin model versions to a rollout policy, we can do gradual ramping with automated rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval set.
[06:45] Ethan: How do you handle prompts that contain PII? We need masking in logs and controlled retention.
[06:53] Carlos: We offer prompt redaction policies and can configure retention windows per customer. For regulated flows we recommend private deployment and shorter retention (default 30 days, configurable).
[07:06] Priya: On legal — do you have a standard amendment template or do we need to propose one?
[07:12] Samir: We'll send our amendment and pricing appendix; your legal can mark it up. If there are material changes we'll loop legal folks on both sides.
[07:21] Maya: Can we get a timeline summary live — bullets of milestones?
[07:27] Samir: Sure: 1) Send amendment + pricing by 2026-08-27; 2) Altair sign/PO by 2026-09-15; 3) EU staging benchmark week of 2026-09-07; 4) Production EU go-live target 2026-10-15 (contingent on PO and peering).
[07:45] Lena: I'll own the staging benchmark and will schedule the scripts, also will include latency and token cost per model.
[07:54] Liam: For the benchmark, can we include real-world chains (multi-turn) and function/tool calling flows? Those are latency heavy.
[08:05] Lena: Yes, include chain-of-thought flows, tool-call mocks and memory KV patterns. We'll also track tail latency during sustained bursts.
[08:18] Maya: Any competing vendors we should be aware of? We evaluated CloudAEndpoint and OpenHost AI earlier, but Redwood's dedicated offering looks better for latency predictability.
[08:30] Samir: Appreciate that. We'll also include a short note comparing dedicated vs hosted economics for your traffic shape.
[08:39] Ethan: One minor nit — your API has a small change from last quarter, the function-calling response now returns a slightly different schema that broke a test. Any docs?
[08:50] Lena: Yes we updated the schema to include a status field. We'll send the migration notes and patch examples.
[08:58] Priya: Anything else on compliance? We need a contact for SOC2 evidence.
[09:04] Carlos: I'll be the point of contact; sharing docs by EOD tomorrow.
[09:10] Maya: Ok let's do a quick recap and then close.
[09:14] Samir: Recap: Samir sends amendment, Lena runs the EU staging benchmark, Carlos shares SOC2/KMS docs, Maya/Priya aim to confirm PO and budget.
[09:25] Maya: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Liam: Thanks — will follow up on a Slack thread for peering details.
[09:32] Samir: Great — we'll loop in legal after we send.
[09:35] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: There are a few mis-heard words (e.g., SAMEL instead of SAML in one segment, K-V cache spelled out mid-transcript). The content above captures the important next steps and technical concerns.
